stories.title: Bitcoin Hits $80,000, Sparking Over $220M in Short Liquidations
stories.summary: Bitcoin rose to $80,000 on August 24, per Cointelegraph. Earlier the same day, CoinDesk reported bitcoin near $78,000, with gold also rallying and altcoins consolidating after their best week in three years. The move to $80,000 triggered more than $220 million in short position liquidations within 24 hours.
stories.whyItMatters: Large, fast liquidations show heavy leverage in the market. This can make price swings sharper in both directions.
whatToWatch: Whether bitcoin holds above $80,000
Further liquidation data over the next 24 hours
Altcoin price action following bitcoin's move
questions: What drove the jump from $78,000 to $80,000 in one day?
How much of the move came from short covering versus new buying?

sources.title: Bitcoin price hits $80K as 24-hour crypto short liquidations pass $220M
Bitcoin steadies near $78,000 as gold rallies, altcoins consolidate after best week in 3 years

stories.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs Grew $23 Billion Last Week — Most Wasn't New Money
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin and ether ETFs grew by $23 billion in total assets last week, per Decrypt. Only about $2.6 billion of that came from new investor inflows. The rest reflected price gains as bitcoin and ether both rallied.
stories.whyItMatters: Rising ETF assets can look like strong demand, but most of this gain came from price, not new buyers. That distinction matters for judging real institutional appetite.
whatToWatch: Next week's ETF flow data
Whether net inflows pick up or continue to lag AUM growth
questions: How is the $2.6 billion split between bitcoin and ether funds?

sources.title: Bitcoin, Ethereum ETFs Grew $23 Billion Last Week—Only $2.6 Billion Was New Money

stories.title: Saylor Sat Out Bitcoin's Rally While Tom Lee Bought Ethereum's Surge
stories.summary: Michael Saylor made no bitcoin purchases during a reported 20% rally in bitcoin's price, per CryptoSlate. At the same time, Tom Lee bought Ethereum after ETH surged about 30%. The contrast points to different bets on which asset has more room to run.
stories.whyItMatters: Saylor and Lee are two closely watched figures in corporate crypto buying. Their diverging moves are a signal readers use to gauge sentiment on bitcoin versus ether.
whatToWatch: Whether Saylor resumes bitcoin purchases
Further Ethereum buys tied to Tom Lee
questions: Why did Saylor pause buying during this rally?
Is Lee's ETH purchase a short-term trade or a longer bet?

sources.title: Saylor sat out Bitcoin’s 20% rally while Tom Lee bought Ethereum after a 30% surge

stories.title: Coinbase Launches Tokenized Stocks on Base Network
stories.summary: Coinbase has launched tokenized stock trading on its Base network, per CoinDesk. This puts Coinbase in a growing field of crypto platforms working to bring traditional equities onto blockchain rails.
stories.whyItMatters: Tokenized stocks could change how equities are traded and settled. Regulators have not fully settled how to treat these products, so this is worth watching.
whatToWatch: Which stocks are available at launch
Regulatory response to Coinbase's tokenized equities
Competing launches from other platforms
questions: What regulatory framework covers these tokenized shares?
Can non-US users access this product?

stories.title: Bitcoin Posts Second-Best Week Since Early 2021 as Rally Broadens
stories.summary: Bitcoin had its second-best week since early 2021, per CoinDesk. The rally came alongside two other trends CoinDesk reported: crypto card spending passed $1 billion, driven partly by stablecoins used for everyday purchases, and AI agents are starting to use stablecoins to pay for services.
stories.whyItMatters: A strong price rally paired with real stablecoin usage growth suggests demand right now is not purely speculative.
whatToWatch: Whether the rally continues into next week
Growth in crypto card spending
Adoption of stablecoin payments by AI agent platforms
questions: How much of the $1 billion in card spending is stablecoins versus other crypto?
Which AI agent platforms are actually using stablecoins today?

stories.title: Strive Buys 1,110 More Bitcoin, Holdings Pass 21,000 BTC
stories.summary: Strive bought 1,110 bitcoin for about $81.5 million, per Cointelegraph. The purchase brings its total holdings above 21,000 BTC. Strive's stock, ASST, rose 11% after the news.
stories.whyItMatters: Strive's continued buying adds to a growing list of public companies holding bitcoin as a treasury asset, a trend that shapes both sentiment and supply.
whatToWatch: Whether Strive makes further purchases
ASST share price over the coming days
questions: How is Strive financing these purchases?

stories.title: Bitcoin Rally Accelerates Toward $80,000 After Strong ETF Week
stories.summary: Bitcoin's rally picked up speed, with the price approaching $80,000, per Bitcoin Magazine. The publication linked the move to a strong week of ETF activity.
stories.whyItMatters: The tie between ETF activity and price action shows how much influence these investment vehicles now have on short-term moves.
whatToWatch: Whether bitcoin breaks and holds above $80,000
Next week's ETF flow figures
questions: How much of this rally is ETF-driven versus other factors?

stories.title: Bitmine Buys Another $81 Million in Ethereum as ETH Outpaces Bitcoin
stories.summary: Bitmine bought another $81 million of Ethereum, per Decrypt. The purchase came as ETH continued to outperform bitcoin in recent trading.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitmine's repeated large ETH purchases point to sustained corporate demand for Ethereum specifically, separate from the broader bitcoin trade.
whatToWatch: Bitmine's total ETH holdings going forward
Whether ETH keeps outperforming bitcoin
questions: What is Bitmine's total ETH position now?

stories.title: Bitget CEO Says She's Skipping the Rally, Waiting for Bitcoin at $50,000
stories.summary: Bitget's CEO said she is not buying into the current bitcoin rally, per Cointelegraph. She said she is waiting for a pullback to $50,000 before she buys.
stories.whyItMatters: A major exchange executive publicly doubting the rally is a contrarian view worth weighing against the bullish mood elsewhere in the market.
whatToWatch: Whether bitcoin pulls back toward $50,000
Other executives' public stances on the rally
questions: What is her reasoning for expecting a drop to $50,000?

stories.title: Solana Vote Could Push Daily SOL Burns to $800,000, Slow New Token Launches
stories.summary: A new Solana governance vote could raise daily SOL token burns to as much as $800,000, per CoinDesk. The change could also slow the creation of new tokens on the network.
stories.whyItMatters: Changes to burn and issuance rules directly affect SOL's supply and the cost of launching new projects on Solana.
whatToWatch: Result of the vote
Timeline for implementation if it passes
Effect on new token launch activity
questions: How would slower token creation affect Solana's developer ecosystem?

stories.title: Fed Study: Bitcoin Rallies Draw In New Buyers Swayed by Recent Returns
stories.summary: A Federal Reserve experiment found that bitcoin rallies attract new crypto buyers, per CoinDesk and Cointelegraph. The study found investor behavior is driven largely by beliefs, and those beliefs shift easily based on recent returns.
stories.whyItMatters: Research from the Fed on retail crypto behavior gives a data-backed look at how momentum, not fundamentals, may drive much of the buying in rallies.
whatToWatch: Whether the Fed publishes further research on this topic
How this finding factors into investor-protection discussions
questions: What methodology did the Fed use?
Does the finding hold for institutional investors too?

sources.title: Fed experiment shows how bitcoin rallies attract new crypto buyers
Fed study finds crypto investors driven by beliefs, easily swayed by returns

stories.title: Ether Outperforms Bitcoin as 'Golden Cross' Points to More Upside
stories.summary: Ether has sharply outperformed bitcoin recently, per CoinDesk. A technical pattern known as a 'golden cross' has formed, which some traders read as a sign the move could continue. This is a technical signal, not a guarantee.
stories.whyItMatters: Technical patterns like this often draw more trading activity, but they have a mixed track record, so readers should treat them as one data point, not a forecast.
whatToWatch: Whether the ETH/BTC ratio keeps rising
Whether the golden cross pattern holds or fails
questions: How reliable has this signal been for ETH in the past?

sources.title: Ether is crushing bitcoin and the 'golden cross' says it may not be done yet
